summary.text: The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System, a massive sphere of hot plasma heated by nuclear fusion in its core.
It is the main source of energy for life on Earth, and its mass makes up about 99.86% of the Solar System's total.
Every second its core fuses about 600 billion kilograms of hydrogen into helium, converting four billion kilograms of matter into energy.

items.prompt: Two marks on the Sun's surface, one at the equator and one near a pole, start a turn together. Which comes round again first?

options.label: The equator mark, since the Sun spins faster there
The pole mark, since it has a shorter path
Both together, as if the Sun were one solid piece
The pole mark, since it sits closer to the core

items.explain: The Sun rotates faster at its equator than at its poles: about 25.6 days against 33.5 days.

items.prompt: A friend says the Sun shines because it burns fuel like a giant bonfire. What is the better description?

options.label: Its surface burns hydrogen in oxygen like a huge flame
Its core fuses hydrogen into helium and turns some matter into energy
Friction from its fast spin heats its plasma
An enormous electric current runs through its centre

items.explain: Nuclear fusion in the core heats the Sun; each second it converts four billion kilograms of matter into energy.

items.prompt: Billions of years from now the Sun's core runs low on the reaction that powers it. What happens to its outer layers?

options.label: They shrink at once into a white dwarf
They stay put while only the core changes
They expand, and the Sun becomes a red giant
They drift off immediately, leaving a black dwarf

items.explain: As hydrogen fusion in the core diminishes, the core grows denser and hotter and the outer layers expand into a red giant. The white dwarf comes after.

items.prompt: The Sun spins, and planets pull on it. What do careful satellite measurements find about its shape?

options.label: It is flattened at the poles because its equator spins faster
It is pulled into an egg shape by the planets
It is uneven, with big bumps where hot gas rises
It is the closest to a perfect sphere of any natural object observed

items.explain: The measured flattening is tiny, about 8 parts per million, and the planets' tidal effect is weak, so the Sun is the most spherical natural object seen.

items.prompt: Astronomers analyse the Sun's visible surface layer to see what it is made of. What do they find most of it is?

options.label: Hydrogen and helium
Oxygen and carbon
Iron and neon
Nitrogen and oxygen, like air

items.explain: The photosphere is mostly hydrogen (about 73%) and helium (about 25%), with much smaller amounts of heavier elements.

items.prompt: Astronomers needed a handy yardstick for distances in the Solar System. What did they base the astronomical unit on?

options.label: The Sun's diameter
The distance between the Sun and the Earth
The distance from Earth to the Moon
The distance from the Sun to the nearest star

items.explain: The distance between the Sun and the Earth was used to define the astronomical unit.

pack.title: Not a Solid Ball
pack.question: What is the Sun made of, how does it shine, and what will become of it?

beats.title: Not a Solid Ball
beats.hook: The star that lights our days has no solid surface to stand on, and it is slowly changing.

beats.prompt: Each second, the Sun's core fuses hydrogen into helium. What becomes of some of the matter in the process?
beats.explain: The Sun's core fuses about 600 billion kilograms of hydrogen into helium each second and converts four billion kilograms of matter into energy.

choices.label: Some of it is converted into energy
Nothing is lost; all the mass leaves as helium
choices.feedback: In everyday life matter is not used up, but here about four billion kilograms of matter every second is converted into something else.

choices.label: It is thrown into space as loose hydrogen gas
choices.feedback: The hydrogen that is fused ends up as helium; it is not simply ejected.

beats.prompt: Put these stages of the Sun's story in order.

items.label: Gas in a molecular cloud collapses
The Sun swells into a red giant
It sheds its outer layers and becomes a white dwarf

beats.explain: The Sun formed from a collapsing cloud, began fusion in its core, will become a red giant, and then shed its layers to become a white dwarf.

beats.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

right.label: The scientific study of the Sun
Where hydrogen is fused into helium

beats.explain: Each term names a part of the Sun or a way people study and measure it.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?

steps.text: The Sun's equator turns once in about 25.6 days.
Its poles take about 33.5 days to turn once.
So the equator turns faster than the poles.
So the whole Sun must turn as one rigid piece, like a solid ball.

beats.explain: Different turning times at the equator and poles mean the Sun has differential rotation, so it does not turn as one rigid piece.

beats.idea: The Sun is a ball of hot plasma powered by fusion in its core, and that fuel supply shapes its long life story.

paragraphs.heading: Our star
paragraphs.text: The Sun is the star at the centre of the Solar System. It is a giant ball of hot plasma, made to glow by nuclear fusion reactions deep in its core. From its surface it gives off that energy mainly as visible light and infrared, with 10% coming out as ultraviolet. Life on Earth runs mainly on the energy it sends us.

paragraphs.heading: Size and distance
paragraphs.text: On average the Sun is about 1.496×10⁸ kilometres from Earth, a distance light covers in about 8 minutes. That distance was used to set a unit of length, the astronomical unit (au). The Sun is the biggest and heaviest thing in the Solar System: about 1,391,400 km across, roughly 109 times Earth's width. Its mass is around 330,000 times Earth's, about 99.86% of all the mass in the Solar System. Its surface layer, the photosphere, is mostly hydrogen (~73%) and helium (~25%), with small amounts of heavier elements such as oxygen, carbon, neon and iron.

paragraphs.heading: How it was born
paragraphs.text: The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago, when matter inside part of a large molecular cloud collapsed under its own gravity. Most of that matter piled up in the middle, while the rest spread into a flat, circling disk that became the Solar System. The central mass grew so hot and dense that fusion eventually switched on in its core.

paragraphs.heading: What kind of star
paragraphs.text: Every second, the core fuses about 600 billion kilograms of hydrogen into helium and turns four billion kilograms of matter into energy. Astronomers class the Sun as a G2V star, a G-type main-sequence star. The 2 means its surface temperature falls in the second range of the G class. With an absolute magnitude of +4.83, it is thought to outshine roughly 85% of the Milky Way's stars, most of which are red dwarfs.

paragraphs.heading: How it will end
paragraphs.text: In about four to seven billion years, hydrogen fusion in the core will fade until the Sun can no longer hold its balance. The core will then grow much denser and hotter, pushing the outer layers outward until the Sun becomes a red giant. Models suggest it will next throw off those outer layers and become a white dwarf, a dense, cooling star that no longer fuses anything but still glows with stored heat, perhaps for trillions of years. After that, it is expected to end as a black dwarf, extremely dense and giving off almost no energy.

paragraphs.heading: Almost perfectly round
paragraphs.text: One measure of the Sun's shape, its oblateness, is very hard to pin down, and because the air distorts the view it has to be measured from satellites. When the Solar Dynamics Observatory and the Picard satellite measured it precisely, the result was smaller than anyone expected: 8.2×10⁻⁶, which is 8 parts per million. That makes the Sun the closest thing to a perfect sphere of any natural object ever observed. Yet it does not spin as one solid piece. Measured against the stars, its equator turns once in about 25.6 days, while its poles take about 33.5 days.
